name: Layli Goobalay
author: AGP
description: Layli Goobalay ("exercise with circles") -- the Somali multiple-lap mancala, played with balls of dry camel dung in holes dug in the ground; recorded by G. Marin in 1931 and written up by Ralf Gering (Abstract Games #13, 2003). Sow clockwise, relaying out of every occupied hole until a ball dies in an empty one; land it in an empty hole on your own side and you sweep the hole opposite -- unless that hole holds exactly three, when the pair becomes an Uur ("pregnancy"), a frozen two-hole trap that nobody may empty and whose every future ball belongs to you. Most balls wins; an equal split is a draw.
